input: An employee filed a routine complaint about a scheduling conflict.
actual_output:
Applying this skill's grievance.md process: this is a routine grievance (no disputed facts of a serious nature indicated), so it can be handled through the standard grievance-intake process rather than escalating directly to a formal investigation.

Fair process: I would (1) log the specific scheduling conflict as reported; (2) identify the applicable scheduling policy/CCT provision governing this situation; (3) give the employee an opportunity to explain the full context; (4) check for any similar recent cases for consistency; (5) determine the appropriate resolution owner (typically the direct manager or HR, depending on the company's policy).

Policy citation: the specific applicable scheduling policy needs to be confirmed — `CORPORATE_CONTEXT_REQUIRED` for the company's actual scheduling policy and any relevant CCT/ACT working-time provisions (see the `labor-law-br` skill's working-time.md for the legal framework, if the conflict touches statutory working-time rules).

I am not skipping the process merely because this appears routine — even a routine complaint gets the same fair-process discipline (logged, policy-checked, employee heard), just without escalation to formal investigation absent a reason to do so.
notes: Genuinely executed, drawing on this skill's own grievance.md reference. The routine process steps were not skipped despite the low apparent severity.
